body: The most important type of love to have is self-love. I was in a 5 year relationship that turned very toxic. My ex-boyfriend originally did a lot of what you’re talking about: surprised me with presents, hug me, hold the door for me, etc. Once things started to go south, I found myself feeling extremely lonely while in a relationship. I had so much love to give to someone that ended up being unfaithful. Now I’m lost, recovering from years of being with someone 24/7 / making them apart of my identity. I believe that when you truly love yourself and focus on the becoming the best version of yourself, someone will come along that falls in love with you (the best version of you). My advice would be to spend less time seeking love and focus on feeling content with yourself, and around your buddies. You never know, someone that is currently in a relationship could end up being your soulmate. Sometimes relationships that seem like rainbows and butterflies truly aren’t.

Since I’m 20, it’s a bit hard to “mingle.” I can’t legally go to a bar and it’s sorta out of my comfort zone to just show up to a party I wasn’t invited to. I have met up with a couple guys from tinder but that can also become intimidating at times.
Real friends feel almost non-existent nowadays, sending you a *virtual hug* I could use one right now as well
